title: Review: ea, oa, ow
parentNote: No new sound today. Just the three teams from the last three days, and the useful thing about them is that they only make two sounds between them: ea says ee, and oa and ow both say oh. So the first question is never which team is it, it is which sound is it — ee or oh. Once your child has sorted a word into the oh pile, the old rule finishes the job: oa sits in the middle (coach, goal, loaf), ow sits on the end (low, pillow, elbow). The slip to expect is a word like loaf being read as leaf, because ea and oa look alike at a glance and the rest of the word is identical. Slow that one down: cover everything but the two vowel letters and ask only ee or oh, then uncover and read. If they are tired, stop after the first story — the second one can wait until tomorrow.

activities.prompt: Three teams from this week. Two of them say oh. Find the one that says ee.
Now the other way round. Two of these say ee. Find the one that says oh.
Sort it first. Is the team in the middle an ee or an oh?
The same ending, but a different team in the middle. This one is the oh.
Still an oh, but the word stops at the team. On the end it is ow.
The long one, and it has both sounds in it. An oh at the front and an ee in the middle.
Three words that start with an l. Listen for ee or oh, and then for the end.
This one is hard. One has a team that says oh, one has a team that says ee, and one has no team at all.
All three begin with an m. Two of them say oh, and only one of those stops at the team.

activities.title: The seal on the beach
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Meg did take a peach and a bag to the beach.
A seal did creep up the sand and did peep at the bag.
It did sneak the peach and did eat the lot in a flash.
Meg did stamp and did tell it to stop.
The seal did flap and did bark back at Meg.
Then it did drop a fat fish on the mat at her feet.
Meg did grin. It is not a peach, but it is a deal.

activities.title: The goat in the rowboat
activities.prompt: A second story, and it is all the oh sound this time.
lines: Bart did load oats and a cloak in the rowboat.
The goat did jump in with him, and the boat did sit low.
Bart did row and row, and the boat did creep on, slow and slow.
Then the goat did eat the oats. Then it did eat the cloak.
Bart did moan. The goat did not.
A crow did land on the goat and did peck at its coat.
Bart did row back to the road. The oats and the cloak sat in the goat.
